slides.title: Pull fiber without breaking it
slides.sub: Tension, lubricant, pull points and swivels

slides.title: Pulling damage hides until the test results.
slides.body: It shows up as an attenuation step, or a broken fiber months later.

slides.title: Know the tension limit
slides.body: Outside plant loose-tube cable is commonly rated 600 lbf, about 2,700 N. Pull on the strength member, never the fibers.

slides.title: Bends multiply tension
slides.body: Friction adds up, but bends multiply it. Put the reel at the end nearest the bends, while the cable is still slack.

slides.title: Lubricate all the way
slides.body: Water-based gel, applied continuously at the feed end. Never grease, oil or dish soap.

slides.title: Swivels stop the twist
slides.body: A swivel keeps tape twist out of the cable. A breakaway swivel's shear pin lets go before the cable's limit.

slides.title: Too long? Figure-eight it
slides.body: Pull to a midpoint handhole, lay the cable out in a figure-eight so it can't twist, then feed it onward.
